transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-16 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Rao (Hydrangea), Tom Bennett (Hydrangea Platform), Clara Liu (Hydrangea Security), Miguel Alvarez (Clinical Ops)

Summary: 6-week POC scoped for triage and entity extraction on clinical lab reports in English + Spanish, with emphasis on domain-specific accuracy and low hallucination. Discussed model shortlist (open model candidates), workload sizing (qps, tokens/day), latency/cost tradeoffs, hosting options (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC), and security checklist. Agreed next steps: bench run, sharing sample data, pricing and security docs.

Topics: success criteria; shortlist models to test; bench plan; multilingual tokenization; quantization tradeoffs; deployment options; timelines and decision gates.

[00:00] Lena (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for hopping on, quick intros then we'll get into the POC goals. Sorry if audio is a bit scratchy, Samir are you on mobile?
[00:12] Samir (Redwood SE): I'm on laptop, slight echo maybe. Hi Priya, Tom, Clara. We looked at the initial form you filled out, had some follow-ups about volume and languages.
[00:22] Priya (Hydrangea): Great, thanks. For context we process lab reports and referral notes. Primary is English, about 20% Spanish, and some fragmented bilingual entries. The core use-case is entity extraction (tests, values, units), triage classification for urgent flags, and a short structured summary for clinicians.
[00:40] Tom: Right and platform constraints — we need p50 latency under 200 ms for short queries in the UI, p95 ideally <1s. Burst tolerance up to 60 QPS for short periods. Daily tokens roughly 3.5 million tokens currently during peak.
[01:05] Samir: Okay that helps. We usually size for steady-state qps and then plan burst capacity on Dedicated pools or hosted autoscale. Do you have SLOs on hallucination rates or extraction recall?
[01:18] Priya: For entity extraction we want recall > 95% for critical fields (test name, value, units), precision > 97 if possible. For triage labels we need F1 > 0.88 on our annotated set. Hallucinations — ideally below 2% on sampled outputs, otherwise clinicians flag.
[01:37] Jordan (Redwood): Good concrete numbers. For the POC we recommend putting together a 500-2k sample deck with ground truth. We can run a bench across models and quantization settings and return latency/cost/quality matrix.
[01:53] Priya: We'll prepare that. On models, we prefer open weights to avoid licensing, and also exploring private deployment later. Any suggestions?
[02:03] Samir: Based on your requirements we'll shortlist 4 open-style candidates: Mistral-Instruct-7B (strong few-shot), OpenLLaMA-30B (solid instruction tuning), Meta Llama-3-70B - flagged as heavy but strong QA performance, and an experimental Mosaic MPT-30B variant we've seen good throughput on. We also suggested one highly quantized 8-bit variant to compare cost.
[02:27] Priya: Llama-3 is attractive but size is a concern for latency, and we have EU data residency questions. We might prefer mix: small decently tuned model for extraction and a larger model only for fallback summaries.
[02:41] Tom: Exactly, we'd probably do a tiered routing: short extraction path to reduce cost, escalate to a richer model if confidence low. Can Redwood support that routing policy?
[02:52] Lena: Yes we have smart routing; you can pin routes to model variants and set fallback policies. The console shows token-level cost and latency per route.
[03:02] Clara: About security — we need SOC2 type II, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and the option for customer-managed KMS. Can you run in our VPC or on-prem?
[03:13] Jordan: We support Private deployments with customer-managed networking and KMS/HSM integrations. For the POC we can start on Hosted with private data handling and then move to Dedicated or Private depending on acceptance.
[03:24] Miguel: Quick question: multilingual tokenization — Spanish medical terms sometimes split badly, and chemical names break tokens. How do models handle that?
[03:33] Samir: Tokenization is model-dependent; smaller models sometimes fragment domain terms more, which impacts generation. We include domain-specific tokens via adapters or we can do short fine-tuning/LoRA to improve consistency. For the bench we'll measure entity token continuity and OOV rates.
[03:51] Priya: Important: we cannot share PHI. We'll de-id samples but want to see how models handle edge cases like shorthand notes.
[03:58] Lena: Totally fine, de-id is fine; also we can sign an NDA or add Data Processing Addendum if needed — we'll share templates.
[04:12] Tom: On workload sizing — our current peak 3.5M tokens/day translates to about 40-50 QPS during peak window — are we expecting 1:1 token to token, or do you account for extra tokens for system prompts and retrieval context?
[04:29] Samir: We always account for system & retrieval overhead. If you run retrieval augmentation with a 512-token context that multiplies tokens. For cost estimates we'll need average prompt+context size — can you estimate?
[04:40] Priya: Typical prompt length for extraction is 80 tokens, but if we add a retrieval chunk it's ~450 tokens. Summaries can be 200-400 prompt tokens.
[04:51] Samir: Perfect. We'll use the 450 token average for routed cases and 80 for pure extraction to size GPUs and expected per-token billing.
[05:00] Jordan: For latency targets we might provision a mix: smaller low-latency model instances (e.g., Mistral 7B quantized) for extraction, and a larger instance pool for fallback. That keeps cost down while meeting p50 SLA.
[05:15] Priya: How long is a typical Redwood POC? We want a clear decision gate.
[05:20] Lena: We usually do 4–6 weeks. Week 0 onboarding and dataset/bench prep, Week 1–2 bench runs and quality matrix, Week 3 iteration (quantize/fine-tune LoRA), Week 4 demo + decision. If you need a deeper private deployment test, extend to 6–8 weeks.
[05:36] Priya: That seems reasonable. Budget is modest — team can commit to a pilot spend but prefer not to commit to large Dedicated until results are in. Pricing and pilot credits will be important.
[05:46] Lena: We'll include pilot credits in the pricing sheet and show Dedicated vs Hosted unit economics.
[05:52] Tom: A technical deep-dive question: when you run quantized models do you preserve KV cache accuracy? We've seen some 8-bit quantization cause degradation for long contexts.
[06:03] Samir: Good point. 8-bit can affect attention kernel numerics and KV stability for very long contexts; for your use (short extraction + medium retrieval) it's often acceptable but we'll benchmark both 8-bit and 4-bit LLMQ variants. We'll also measure p95 tail latency with continuous batching enabled.
[06:20] Miguel: Also note that we have regulatory window for EU clinics, so we might need data residency. Can Redwood spin up a regional endpoint?
[06:28] Lena: Yes we have region routing and can host in EU regions or on Private VPC. We'll note regional routing as a must-have for later stages.
[06:36] Priya: On quality tradeoffs — are you able to run hallucination-oriented tests? We have an internal metric where we seed prompts with ambiguous lab codes to test model hallucination.
[06:47] Samir: Absolutely. We'll include a hallucination test set and measure frequency per 1k requests. We'll report both automated metrics and sample outputs for human review.
[06:58] Clara: Please include audit logs and request-level tracing in the POC so security can sample.
[07:05] Jordan: Audit logs and tracing hooks are available in the console; we can provide token-level cost/latency traces tied to request ids for your audit.
[07:13] Priya: Great. Any red flags about model choices? We worry about licensing if we move to production with certain open models.
[07:21] Samir: We always review model licenses — some weights have restrictions. We'll flag any licensing concerns in the bench deliverable. For production, if licensing is an issue we can migrate to a similar Redwood-verified variant.
[07:33] Tom: Okay let's confirm the shortlist to test in the bench.
[07:36] Priya: Please suggest a shortlist and we can veto.
[07:39] Samir: Proposed shortlist for bench: Mistral-Instruct-7B-quant, OpenLLaMA-30B-instruct, Llama-3-70B-capped (hosted to compare output quality), Mosaic MPT-30B-tuned, and a compact ensemble path using an in-house distilled 3B candidate for fastest extraction. We'll also test LoRA fine-tune on top two models with your 500-sample seed.
[08:05] Priya: Sounds good. Add a smaller distilled model — we want to see cost/latency sweet spots.
[08:09] Samir: Will do. We'll produce a matrix: quality (F1/recall), hallucination rate, p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and deployment notes (quantization robustness, region support, license flags).
[08:23] Lena: Timeline recap: We'll get pricing and pilot offer in next 2 days, Samir runs bench in ~5 business days after samples are received, then 1 week for iterations and demo — overall 4 weeks for decision gate.
[08:36] Priya: That aligns.
[08:40] Tom: One more infra note: we need to integrate with our secrets manager and KMS. Which providers do you support?
[08:47] Jordan: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and partner HSMs via standard interfaces. For the POC we can use hosted with customer-managed keys.
[08:58] Clara: We'll share the security questionnaire and require encryption at rest/in flight and audit logs. Also SAML SSO for console access.
[09:06] Lena: We'll include the SOC2 report and a sample DPA with the security pack.
[09:10] Miguel: Quick ops question — do you persist user queries by default? We need data retention to be configurable.
[09:16] Jordan: Retention is configurable; for POC we can disable logging of payloads or restrict retention. We'll document options.
[09:24] Priya: Ok let's close with explicit next steps.
[09:27] Lena: Recap: 1) Hydrangea to share de-id 500 sample set + labels (Priya) 2) Redwood to run 2k-sample bench across shortlist (Samir) 3) Redwood to share pricing and pilot offer (Lena) 4) Hydrangea security questionnaire returned (Clara). We'll set a follow-up bench review for week of Mar 22-26.
[09:48] Priya: Confirmed. Thanks everyone.
[09:51] Tom: Thanks.
[09:52] Meeting end.

Inline notes: occasional transcription artifacts: "V-P-C" for VPC; "K-V cache" sometimes written as K-V cache; several proper nouns like MPT/Mosaic misheard as "Mosaic-MPT". References shared: pricing sheet (link), security pack PDF (link), bench template spreadsheet (link).
